readOnlyRole.title: Use a read-only role
readOnlyRole.body: During setup Adminium reads schema metadata only — never your rows. We recommend a dedicated user with SELECT-only grants; you can decide where Adminium keeps its own tables in the meta-storage step.

capability.mysqlApproxRows: MySQL row counts are storage-engine estimates (they can drift up to ±40%) — shown with ≈.
capability.mysqlFkEnum: MySQL FK/enum metadata is weaker: MyISAM tables declare no foreign keys, enums are per-column enum(…) types, and CHECK constraints need MySQL 8.0.16+ / MariaDB 10.2+.
capability.sqliteCheckEnums: SQLite has no native enum type — enums are synthesized from CHECK (col IN (…)) constraints.
capability.sqliteNoComments: SQLite has no column comments — use the schema remap editor to add labels.
capability.importNoRowCounts: Schema files carry no row counts — the tables list shows — instead of made-up numbers.
capability.importNoLiveHealth: No live database connection — health checks and schema-drift detection are unavailable for this source.
capability.rowsUnavailable: Schema files have no live database — row counts are unknown until you connect one.
capability.rowsRunAnalyze: No estimate yet — run ANALYZE on the database for row counts.
capability.rowsNoEstimate: The engine reported no estimate for this table.
capability.rowsApproximate: Storage-engine estimate — can drift up to ±40% on InnoDB.

byo.heading: No key? Use your own AI tool
byo.subtitle: The copy-paste round-trip — nothing leaves this machine.
byo.body: Studio can generate a self-contained prompt from your schema. Run it in Claude Code, ChatGPT, or any tool you like, then paste the JSON it returns back into the connect wizard. Same validation, same review, same result as the direct path.
byo.guarantee1: The prompt carries only your schema and aggregate stats — never row data by default.
byo.guarantee2: No credentials, instance URL, or identifiers are embedded.
byo.guarantee3: BYO runs make zero network calls.
byo.headingRecommended: Use your own AI tool — no key needed

meta.title: Where should Adminium keep its own tables?
meta.subtitle: Pages, roles, audit log and settings live in adminium_-prefixed tables — never mixed into your data.

sameDb.title: Same database
sameDb.description: adminium_* tables are created beside your source tables. Simplest setup — needs a role with write and CREATE TABLE privileges.
sameDb.disabledReadOnly: Your role is read-only — Adminium never writes to this database. Choose a separate database for Adminium’s own tables.
sameDb.disabledNoDdl: This role cannot run DDL — Adminium migrations need CREATE TABLE. Choose a separate database for Adminium’s own tables.
sameDb.disabledFile: A schema file has no live database — choose a separate database for Adminium’s own tables.

separate.title: Separate database
separate.description: Adminium keeps its tables in a different database. Your source stays untouched — required for read-only sources.
separate.helper: Needs write + DDL privileges — Adminium runs its own migrations there.
separate.insufficient: This role cannot host the meta store — Adminium needs write and CREATE TABLE privileges there.

v1Note.title: About this install
v1Note.body: This server already keeps its own tables in a configured database, and this step does not move them. It validates that your choice is compatible with this connection — the server enforces the same rule independently (409 META_PLACEMENT_INVALID).

move.title: Moving Adminium’s tables
move.copyingBody: Copying every adminium_ table into the new database. Your source data is not touched, and nothing is switched over until the copy is verified.
move.restartingBody: The copy is done. Adminium is restarting onto the new database — this page will continue by itself in a few seconds.
move.failed: Could not move Adminium’s tables — retry.
move.timeout: Adminium moved its tables but has not come back yet. Your data is safe in the new database — reload this page in a moment.

willMove.title: This will move Adminium’s tables
willMove.body: Adminium is currently using its built-in SQLite store. Continue copies that store into the database you picked and restarts onto it — accounts, pages and settings come with it, so you stay signed in.

intent.title: What do you need?
intent.subtitle: The intent shapes which pages get generated. You can change it later — changing it proposes a regeneration, never a silent rewrite.
intent.trust: We read your schema only — never your row data during setup.

fullAdmin.title: Full admin panel
fullAdmin.description: Dashboards, CRUD pages, search, imports and exports — everything your schema supports.

analytics.title: Read-only analytics
analytics.description: Dashboards, charts and read-only grids. No forms, no writes — every role capped at Viewer.

crud.title: CRUD tables
crud.description: One editing page per table plus search and import/export — a minimal home, no dashboards.

support.title: Support console
support.description: Queues, ticket and customer detail pages first. Deletes off by default. (Queue templates land in M7 — the v1 page set matches Full admin.)

generate.title: Generate your app
generate.subtitle: One page per included table plus dashboards per domain — intent:
generate.successBody: {pages} pages across {groups} navigation groups — generated from your schema, editable in Studio.
generate.failed: Generation failed — retry, or re-run introspection first.
generate.fileTitle: Schema file parsed — generation needs a live database
generate.fileBody: Your schema parsed cleanly and the preview above is real. Generating a running app straight from a schema file (with placeholder rows) is not available yet — connect a live database to generate today.

column.logicalTypeHelper: Inferred: {type} (from {dbType}) — mapped by the adapter; not overridable in v1.
column.currencyHelper: ISO 4217 code applied to money formatting.
column.piiHelper: Masked values render redacted; unmasking requires the data.unmask_pii permission and is audit-logged.
column.enumHelper: Workflow enums drive status pills and board columns; tones map values onto the semantic tint scale.

table.navGroupHelper: Nav placement is decided by the generator — a table.navGroup override is not in the v1 vocabulary.
table.includeHelper: Excluded tables get no pages and disappear from nav.
table.shapeHelper: Classification is recomputed on every introspection; overrides layer on top and survive regeneration.

relations.noneDeclared: No declared foreign keys touch this table.

toast.savedDetail: The applied schema below reflects your changes.

noDesign.schemaFile: This connection was created from a schema file, so there is no database to change. Labels and relations still work.

scopes.deleteBody: Any page using a key bound to this scope stops loading data. Keys are not deleted — revoke them first if that is what you meant.
scopes.deletePrompt: Type the scope name to confirm
scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.subtitle: A scope is the whole of what a key may reach — the tables, the exact columns, and a filter the caller can narrow but never remove.
scopes.emptyBody: Create one below. It is checked against your live schema before it is saved.
scopes.keyCount: {count, plural, =0 {no keys} one {# key} other {# keys}}
scopes.documentHint: Compiled against your schema when you save. Every column a caller can reach is listed here and nowhere else. A default may be '{'"$generate": "uuid"'}' or '{'"$generate": "now"'}' — the server fills those in on create, so a visitor can add a row without choosing its id.

publicApi.title: Public API
publicApi.subtitle: Let your own customer- or staff-facing pages read this database, through a scope you define.

notRegistered.title: Not enabled on this server
notRegistered.body: Set ADMINIUM_PUBLIC_API_ORIGINS to the exact origins allowed to call it, then restart. Until then these routes are not served at all.

toggle.label: Serve the public API
toggle.hint: Turning this off stops every public request immediately. Nothing is deleted — keys, scopes and data all survive.

keys.title: Keys
keys.subtitle: These go in your page’s JavaScript, so anyone can read them. That is expected — a key can only ever do what its scope allows.
keys.emptyBody: Create a scope first, then mint a key for it.
keys.scopeIsAuthTitle: The scope is the only permission
keys.scopeIsAuthBody: A key can reach exactly what its scope lists and nothing else. It does not use roles or table permissions, and it cannot read anything through the rest of the API.
keys.appLabel: Bind to a hosted app surface (optional)
keys.appHint: The app’s customer surface then serves this key itself — rotating it needs no rebuild.

hostedApps.title: Hosted apps
hostedApps.subtitle: The app surfaces this instance serves — where each one appears, and the domains pointed at them.
hostedApps.emptyTitle: No app surfaces are being served
hostedApps.emptyBody: Point ADMINIUM_SURFACES_DIR at a directory of built surfaces — one folder per app and side, each with its index.html — and restart. They are then served under /apps/ and appear here.

surfaces.title: Surfaces
surfaces.subtitle: A staff surface can blend into this dashboard’s sidebar or stand on its own; a customer surface is public and reads through its bound key.
surfaces.noNav: Internal placement unavailable — rebuild this surface with the current toolkit so it emits surface.json.
surfaces.noKey: No key bound — this surface cannot read data until one is minted for it.

domains.title: Domains
domains.subtitle: Point a domain’s DNS at your proxy, pass the Host header through to Adminium, and attach it here — that host then serves the surface instead of this dashboard. Certificates stay on your proxy.
domains.savedBody: Mappings take effect within a few seconds. A host only answers once its DNS and your proxy actually reach this instance.

instances.title: Instances
instances.body: Serve the same app over more than one database. Each instance is reachable at /apps/<app>/<segment>/<side>/ and reads only the connection you give it.

file.multipleHelp: The column stores a list of files instead of one. Existing single values keep working — they read as a list of one.

attachments.acceptHint: Choosing none accepts everything this workspace allows. A choice here can only narrow that list, never widen it.

attachments.maxCountHint: Leave empty to accept as many as a record needs.

column.label: Column that holds the files

column.wrongType: This table already has a column with that name, and it cannot hold a file reference. Pick another name.

attachments.enableHintSidecar: Files are linked on Adminium’s side instead. They appear on each record’s page, not in the New dialog.

confirm.title: Apply a destructive change
confirm.body: This change discards data or removes an object. Adminium cannot undo it.

error.identifier: Use lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter.

help.title: What these fields mean
help.subtitle: Plain-language descriptions of each setting, and what it changes for the people using your app.

type.what: What kind of information the field holds — words, whole numbers, money, a date, a yes/no answer. Picking the right one is what lets Adminium show a date picker instead of a text box, and add up a column of money.
type.example: A phone number is usually text, not a number — numbers drop leading zeros.

required.what: The field must be filled in. A row cannot be saved while it is empty.
required.example: An order needs a customer, so that field is required. A delivery note is optional, so it is not.

unique.what: No two rows may hold the same value. The database refuses the second one.
unique.example: Two customers should not share an email address — mark it unique and they cannot.

primaryKey.what: The field that identifies each row — the one Adminium uses to tell one row from another. Every table should have exactly one, and it is almost always the "id" field created for you.
primaryKey.example: Without a primary key, Adminium can list the rows but cannot edit or delete an individual one.

link.what: Connects this row to a row in another table, and asks the database to keep the connection honest — you cannot point at something that is not there.
link.example: A reservation links to a client. Adminium then shows the client on the reservation, and the reservations on the client.

design.unrepresentableDefaults: These columns keep a database-generated default Adminium cannot edit here, and it is left as it is: {columns}

adopt.offer: A new table does nothing until it has a page. Add {tables} to your app?
adopt.grants: No role is given access automatically — grant it in Settings → Roles.
adopt.skippedEdited: Left untouched because you edited them: {pages}.
adopt.everything: This connection already shows every table, so nothing had to be included.
adopt.forbidden: Your role can change the schema but not generate pages. Ask an admin with connection management to add these tables to the app.

ceiling.notYours: {table} holds over {rows} rows. Only a Super Admin can authorise a rewrite this large — ask one, or run the change during a maintenance window with your own tooling.

storage.title: Storage
storage.subtitle: Where this instance keeps uploaded files, exports and other stored bytes.

move.startedBody: It runs in the background as job {jobId} and keeps going if you leave this page. The counts below change as files arrive — reload to see them.
move.title: Move files
move.subtitle: Copies every file from one destination to another and then forgets the old copy. Downloads keep working throughout.
move.kindsHelp: Leave everything unticked to move all of them. Uploads are the files people attach; the rest are artifacts Adminium made.

loadFailed.title: Destinations could not be loaded
loadFailed.forbidden: Changing where files are stored needs the “Manage storage” permission. Ask an administrator to grant it to one of your roles.

delete.blockedBody: {name} still holds {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}. Move them to another destination first, then delete it.
delete.title: Delete this destination
delete.body: Adminium forgets {name} and its credential. Nothing stored in it is touched — the bucket or server itself is yours, and files still recorded against it will refuse the delete.

list.title: Destinations
list.subtitle: New files go to the default destination. Existing files stay where they are until you move them.

test.unreachable: The test could not be run

storage.defaultBlockedByDisabled: A disabled destination cannot be the default. Enable it first.

editor.subtitle: Adminium reads and writes through this destination on your behalf; it is infrastructure you control.

field.name: Name
field.driverLocked: Changing the kind of a destination that already holds files would leave those files unreachable.
field.rootHelper: An absolute path this server can write to — a mounted volume or a network share. Not the default directory, which is already the first entry in the list.
field.presetHelper: Fills in the endpoint, region and addressing style. Anything the provider cannot know about your account is left blank for you to type.
field.endpointDerived: Leave empty for AWS itself — the endpoint follows from the region.
field.pathStyleToggle: Address the bucket as a path rather than a hostname
field.urlHelper: The collection Adminium writes into, as your server publishes it.
field.prefixHelper: A folder inside the destination. Two destinations on one bucket that differ only here share the bucket without sharing a namespace.
field.publicBaseUrlHelper: Optional. Where these objects are readable without Adminium — a CDN in front of a public bucket. Used only when a column stores a link.
field.secretKept: A key is stored. Leave both fields blank to keep it; fill in both to replace it.

secret.partialTitle: Half a credential is not a credential
secret.partialBody: Fill in both fields to replace the stored credential, or clear both to keep it. Saving one alone would quietly keep the old one.
